name: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
problem: W8A8 activation quantization of LLMs is blocked by a small number of activation outlier channels that blow up the per-tensor dynamic range.
mechanism: Difficulty migration via a per-input-channel smoothing factor s: X_hat = X / s and W_hat = W * s (s folded into the preceding LayerNorm / RMSNorm weights so there is no runtime cost), chosen as s_j = max(|X_j|^alpha) / max(|W_j|)^(1-alpha). Activation outliers are squeezed toward the bulk; weight outliers are made slightly worse but weights tolerate that. alpha trades accuracy for hardware ease - alpha=0.5 is the mobile-tuned default, alpha=0.8 maximizes INT8 GPU gains.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract/tables, A100-class GPUs): W8A8 INT8 quantization of OPT-175B, BLOOM-176B and GLM-130B with 'negligible' accuracy loss at up to 1.56x speedup and 2x memory reduction over FP16, using only 128 calibration samples. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4x combined (16-bit weights + 16-bit activations -> 8+8). QUALITY COST: the 175B-class results are near-lossless; the small-model INT8 results in the same paper are where the WikiText perplexity deltas become visible, and those are NOT free.
